summary.intent: Plan and execute Phase 68.2 (SDK-owned read chain and resolved folder listings) for CipherBox end-to-end via GSD workflows — research, scope resolution, planning, verification, then wave-based execution — while also spinning up an independent worktree for Phase 69 (Rust/FUSE) planning.
summary.outcome: Phase 68.2 planning completed (12 plans/7 waves, research, VALIDATION.md, pattern map, plan-checker PASS, coverage gates 13/13) and committed; execution proceeded sequentially through Wave 6 start (10/12 plans done, plan 11 dispatched) with spot-checks after every plan, a REQUIREMENTS.md tracking bug caught and fixed, a planner coverage gap (unowned components/importers blocking Plan 11's deletions) discovered and worked around, and a poll-invalidation test gap closed by Plan 09's executor. A separate git worktree for Phase 69 was created off origin/main.

repo: The GSD plan-phase workflow's UI capability gate only fires when a `ui` hook is actually active in plan:pre hooks for the phase — the lower-level `ui-plan-gate` check can report `block:true` even when no gate should apply; only trust it if a UI hook is present in activeHooks.

GSD executors marking requirement checkboxes `[x]` in REQUIREMENTS.md can be premature when a requirement's acceptance criteria span multiple later plans (e.g. SDK-READ-01/02 were marked complete by plans 01/02 despite depending on deletions that only land in plan 11) — must be reverted to `[ ]` and re-marked at true completion.

Deleting shared services (ipns.service.ts, file-metadata.service.ts, kind-cache.ts, useFileSize.ts) in this phase had a much wider import surface (~15+ importers) than the plans explicitly owned — components like FileList.tsx, DetailsDialog.tsx, TextEditorDialog.tsx, useStreamingPreview.ts, useFileVersions.ts, version-transforms, and useFileOperations.ts needed migration before deletion could be safe.

resolveChildren in packages/sdk/src/folder-listing.ts (lines ~75-81) intentionally skips per-child resolve/unseal failures for availability, but this is security-sound because the parent folder is already gated via ensureFolderLoaded/dfsFindFolder before resolveChildren runs — an attacker cannot get stale/unverified content rendered.

The ROT-07 anti-rollback gate (RotationHighWater.enforceResolved) was previously only wired into the SDK's write path (client.ts:1156) and had zero gating on the read path — Plan 01 added it at client.ts:781 (root resolve) and :913 (dfsFindFolder child loop).

worktree.baseRef config controls whether parallel executor worktrees fork from `head` (carrying all committed PLAN.md files) vs `fresh`/origin/main (which would miss them) — must be verified before dispatching worktree-based executors.

pnpm monorepo worktree executors each need their own `pnpm install`, which is expensive per worktree; for phases with mostly single-plan waves, running sequentially on the main tree (reusing installed node_modules) is more robust than parallel worktree execution.

code.finding: Docstring explains resolveChildren's graceful per-child failure skip is safe because the target folder is already gated before this runs; omitted children are an availability tradeoff, not a security regression.

workflow: gsd-tools commit helper has a known false-negative: it can report `commit_failed` even when the commit verifiably lands in git log — always verify via `git log` rather than trusting the reported status (recorded again here for VALIDATION.md, REQUIREMENTS.md, and the final metadata commit).

When an executor reports a 'notable deviation' on security-adjacent code, spot-check by reading the actual implementation and independently re-running the security-relevant tests rather than trusting the self-report summary alone.

ScheduleWakeup delay must be computed from the actual current time at the moment of scheduling, not an earlier cached timestamp — a quota interruption between computing the delay and calling the tool caused a wake to be scheduled ~25 minutes late; always re-fetch current time immediately before calling ScheduleWakeup.

A stray/incorrect ScheduledWakeup that can't be cleanly retracted is generally harmless if the agent's session context persists across it — the agent can recognize the work is already done and treat the firing as a no-op instead of double-dispatching.

Before large deletion-plans (e.g. removing shared modules and running an allowlist-free grep gate), run a comprehensive residual-importer audit first — the plan's own PLAN.md task 1 may already anticipate the need to re-grep and rewire missed importers, but the actual list of files needing migration can be non-trivial and worth mapping in detail before dispatch.
